events.name: Bengal Famine
events.description: The first major famine under British East India Company rule, exacerbated by high taxation, hoarding, and export policies during a drought, leading to mass starvation and disease.

events.name: Madras Famine
events.description: Famine in the Madras Presidency caused by drought and British policies favoring cash crops and exports, resulting in widespread starvation.

events.name: Chalisa Famine
events.description: Severe famine in northern India due to drought, affecting Delhi and surrounding areas, worsened by colonial exploitation.

events.name: Doji Bara (Skull) Famine
events.description: Famine in Hyderabad and southern Maratha regions, named for unburied skulls, caused by drought and war, with British indirect involvement through alliances.

events.name: Agra Famine
events.description: Famine in northwestern provinces due to drought, with inadequate relief from British authorities.

events.name: Upper Doab Famine
events.description: Famine in the Upper Doab region of North-Western Provinces, exacerbated by British land revenue demands.

events.name: Orissa Famine
events.description: Famine in Orissa due to drought and failed monsoons, with British laissez-faire policies delaying relief, leading to high mortality.

events.name: Rajputana Famine
events.description: Famine in Rajputana and Ajmer-Merwara, caused by drought and inadequate infrastructure.

events.name: Bihar Famine
events.description: Famine in Bihar mitigated somewhat by British relief efforts, but still caused distress due to crop failure.
events.death_toll: Minimal direct deaths due to relief

events.name: Great Famine (Southern India Famine)
events.description: Widespread famine across southern India, worsened by British export policies and inadequate relief, leading to mass migration and deaths.

events.name: Indian Famine
events.description: Famine affecting large parts of India due to drought, with British relief criticized as insufficient.

events.name: Indian Famine
events.description: Another severe famine shortly after the previous, affecting Bombay Presidency and other areas, with high mortality.

events.name: Bombay Presidency Famine
events.description: Famine in Bombay Presidency due to crop failure.

events.name: Excess Deaths from Colonial Policies
events.description: Broad period of elevated mortality due to British economic policies, deindustrialization, and resource drain, leading to chronic malnutrition and vulnerability to crises.

events.name: Suppression of the Indian Revolt
events.description: Brutal suppression of the Indian Rebellion of 1857, involving mass executions, village burnings, and reprisals against civilians.

events.name: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
events.description: British troops under General Dyer fired on unarmed protesters in Amritsar, killing hundreds and injuring thousands.

events.name: Bengal Famine
events.description: Man-made famine during WWII, caused by British wartime policies, food exports, and hoarding, leading to mass starvation despite no major crop failure.

events.name: Indentured Labor System
events.description: System of coerced labor exporting millions of Indians to British colonies, with high mortality during transport and on plantations, often compared to slavery.

events.name: Partition of India
events.description: Hasty British division of India leading to communal violence, mass migrations, and killings.

events.name: Criminal Tribes Act
events.description: Law declaring certain tribes 'criminal by birth,' leading to persecution, forced labor, and internment.
